title: My attempt on a fully fledged ARPG made by AI
author: Defc0ns
selftext:
I've seen some great games made by AI so far, and ive always wanted to develop my own game, so i jumped at it about a month or two ago. Im a vivid fan of the ARPG genre so that was a clear choice for what to build, and as expected i ran into alot of challenges, especially with models, art and animations.

Most AI-built games posted here seem to be pretty small, simple mechanics mostly. I wanted to see what happens if you point the same setup at something with actual systems depth. So: Dreadmark, an ARPG with real itemization, a rune-based skill system and a seasonal multiplayer ladder.

How it works: i do the design and call every decision, the agent writes the implementation. It also plays the game itself with multiple bots to catch regressions before i even see a build. Going forward i want to scale that up into a proper bot-fleet for balance tuning and QA too, but honestly right now most of the work is just getting the bots good enough to trust for that, still very much in progress.

Right now that's two classes, three skill trees each, and multiple runes per skill that actually change what a skill does instead of just buffing numbers, plus a full crafting/affix system. Art and animation are bought assets i hand-integrate, that part's not something the AI does well yet.

The plan going forward is to keep building this with the community, taking suggestions seriously and staying collaborative, with AI doing the heavy lifting but me making every final call.

Heading to Steam Next Fest in October. Curious what people here think of it, does it hold up, or are there tells that give away how it was made. Can go into more detail on the process if anyone wants.
